questions.q: An investigator needs the test results recorded when a lot of glucose strips was released. Which system usually holds them?
options: The PLM
The MES or paper device history record
The CRM
The regulatory submission tool, since it holds the 510(k) test data
questions.why: Production and release records for each lot live in the MES or the paper device history record.

questions.q: Which system is usually the system of record for a device's bill of materials and engineering change orders?
options: PLM, such as Windchill or Agile
MES
The complaint mailbox
The ERP, since it holds every part and its cost for the whole company
questions.why: PLM holds parts, BOMs, drawings, specifications and engineering changes.

questions.q: A new device is substantially equivalent to one already legally sold in the US. Which route to market fits most often?
options: PMA
EU technical file
No submission is ever needed
questions.why: A 510(k) shows substantial equivalence to a legally marketed predicate device.

questions.q: The same product shows up as a part number in PLM, a material number in ERP and a lot in MES. What does this mean for an AI project?
options: Nothing, the model will work it out
Use only one system and ignore the others, since the model can infer the links from product names
Ask users to type all three by hand
Mapping keys across systems is a large share of the work
questions.why: Matching keys across systems is often the hardest data work on MedTech projects.

questions.q: You are writing the checklist for a complaint handling gap assessment. Which statement is written well?
options: Complaints are handled properly
Every complaint has a documented reportability decision with a reason
The process is efficient and complaints are handled to a high standard by trained staff
Staff try their best
questions.why: Checklist statements must be plain and testable against records.

questions.q: A colleague wants to mark a gap because an investigator said the process is slow. What is missing?
options: Evidence such as records or timestamps
A larger font in the table
A vendor quote
Nothing, if the investigator is senior enough the opinion counts as evidence
questions.why: Never mark a gap without evidence from records, timestamps or observation.

questions.q: Which gap is the best candidate for an AI assistant?
options: A form is missing one mandatory field that investigators often forget to fill
Staff were never trained on the procedure
Service emails are re-typed into the QMS, hundreds a month
The procedure has a typo
questions.why: High volume, unstructured text and a quick human check make a good AI fit; the others are fixed by form changes or training.

questions.q: An AI tool would save time but write complaint records outside the QMS. How should the gap assessment treat it?
options: As a clear win, since time saved is the measure the sponsor will report upward
As out of scope
As a matter for IT only
As a net loss, it creates a new compliance gap
questions.why: Efficiency and compliance gaps belong in one list; a new compliance gap cancels the gain.

questions.q: A CAPA is open for 90 days but people work on it for 12 hours in total. Which number drives time saved?
options: The 12 hours of touch time
The 90 days of cycle time
Both added together
Neither, use the number of CAPAs opened per year multiplied by the CAPA board time
questions.why: Time saved comes from touch time; cycle time is a separate quality measure.

questions.q: The sponsor asks you to put a dollar value on avoided warning letters. What is the better approach?
options: Use an industry average cost of a warning letter that you remember from a conference talk
Show the effect in the quality team's own measures unless finance gives a figure
Multiply recalls by a guess
Leave quality out of the case
questions.why: Rare events vary hugely in cost; use the client's own measures or finance's own figure.

questions.q: Which cost do teams most often forget in a MedTech AI value case?
options: Licence fees for the developer tools used to write the pilot code
The pilot build
Re-testing under change control after model or prompt changes
Meeting room booking
questions.why: Change control and re-testing recur with every meaningful change and can make a cheap pilot expensive to keep.

questions.q: How should you present the value case?
options: One exact number
Only the high case
Only the money, since quality measures cannot be compared across clients
Low, likely and high cases with assumptions labeled
questions.why: Ranges with labeled assumptions are more honest and easier to defend.

questions.q: Who can stop any tool that touches a regulated record at a device maker?
options: Quality assurance
The marketing team
The model provider, under its acceptable use policy for regulated industries
The newest user
questions.why: QA approves anything that touches the quality system, so involve them early.

questions.q: Before a first meeting you want to know whether the FDA has cited the client. Where do you look?
options: The 510(k) database
The FDA Warning Letters page
The product classification database
The client's careers page
questions.why: The Warning Letters page shows whether and for what the FDA has cited a company.

questions.q: You found two recent recalls for the client. How should you use this?
options: Open the meeting by naming them
Ignore them completely, since recalls are confidential and must not be read before signing an NDA
Use them to choose your first questions
Post them in the project chat
questions.why: Public data is context to shape questions, not a point to make.

questions.q: Before proposing a custom build for CAPA summaries, what should you check?
options: The client's office location
The model's release date
Whether a larger model would write better CAPA summaries
What the client's QMS vendor already offers or plans
questions.why: The existing validated platform may already offer or soon offer the feature.

questions.q: Which GAMP 5 category usually needs the most specification and testing effort?
options: Category 3, non-configured product
Category 5, custom software
Category 1, infrastructure
Category 4, configured product
questions.why: Effort rises from category 3 to 5 because the more you write, the more you must specify and test.

questions.q: Why is configuring the client's validated QMS often the cheapest option to validate?
options: The platform's validation already exists and you extend it
Configuration never needs testing
Vendors take legal responsibility for validation once the client signs the licence
QMS tools have no audit trail
questions.why: You build on the existing validated state rather than starting from zero.

questions.q: A vendor AI tool updates its model monthly without notice. What is the main concern?
options: The vendor's logo may change
Each update means the client must file a new 510(k) for the QMS
Each update is an uncontrolled change to a validated process
Monthly updates are always free
questions.why: Unannounced model changes shift outputs and break the validated state.

questions.q: In the common hybrid pattern, where do the regulated record and signature stay?
options: In the custom AI service
In the custom AI service database, so drafts and signatures are kept together
In the model provider's logs
In the validated QMS or PLM
questions.why: The custom service drafts; the validated platform keeps the record, signature and audit trail.
